transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: IPTC METAWATCH, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a free and open public monitoring tool that tracks how news publishers handle photo metadata.' Four features: monthly crawls, over 500 publishers in 122 countries, the fields tracked (credits, captions, copyright notices, Exif, IPTC and XMP), a per-field breakdown. Six cards, five the IPTC's (the announcement of 5 October 2026, the overview, the per-field page, a September events post, the photo-metadata archive), one LinkedIn post by Paul Melcher dated 14 September 2026.
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview names the maker, the method and the scale of a monitor three weeks old, and points to its breakdown by field.
findings: THE METHOD AND THE SCALE RIGHT. 'Every month', 'more than 500 news publishers in 122 countries' and the fields are the announcement's own (the census quotes 508 publishers and up to 20 recent articles each). 'Free and open' matches the record's licence quote: every run is published as open data under CC BY 4.0. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the entity pages it saved.

THE FINDINGS ABSENT. The monitor exists to say what survives: in the October run 7.2% of editorial images carried a credit or copyright notice (8% in IMATAG's 2018 test), 321 of the 425 publishers it could crawl kept none of the scored IPTC fields, 27 of 6,580 images carried a C2PA manifest. The composition gives what the monitor checks and none of what it found.

THE DATE. The record dates the monitor by its announcement, 5 October 2026. Two cards date it earlier: an IPTC post of 8 September 2026 in which Brendan Quinn 'appeared again to introduce Metawatch', and Paul Melcher's LinkedIn post of 14 September 2026 ('now publishes Metawatch'). The record's lifecycle is 'announced 5 October 2026'; the first public showing in September is carried here and is unchecked against the posts themselves.
THE ACCESS LIMIT ABSENT. The announcement's note that AP and USA Today began blocking automated access in October, 'bot-blocking aimed at AI also shuts out research', is not composed.
analysis: A new provenance monitor is composed at the grain of its feature list. What the monitor measures is the erasure of credit in the publishing pipeline; the composition carries the instrument and leaves out its reading. The pattern is the IPTC photo metadata capture's in small: the carrier composed, the loss omitted.
per_note: The IPTC named; Paul Melcher and Brendan Quinn appear only in cards; no identifier; the monitor's own pages cited.
